quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2026 revenue exceeded expectations at $225 million, up 4% sequentially and 6% year-over-year, as demand that accelerated in fiscal Q4 continued. IC revenue of $165 million rose 7% year-over-year; high-end IC revenue hit a second consecutive quarterly record at $71 million (up 19%), driven by strength in Asia ahead of Chinese New Year; mainstream IC was flat at $94 million. U.S. revenue increased slightly year-over-year and is expected to contribute to growth over the coming year.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $225 million (+4% sequential, +6% YoY); IC $165 million (+7%); high-end IC $71 million (+19%, record); mainstream IC $94 million (flat)

quarterly_data.signal: Gross margin was at the high end of expectations at 35% on higher revenue and a greater mix of high-end IC revenue; operating margin 24%; GAAP diluted EPS $0.74 and non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.61. Operating cash flow of $97 million (43% of revenue) was the second highest quarter in company history.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 35%; operating margin 24%; GAAP EPS $0.74 / non-GAAP $0.61; operating cash flow $97 million (43% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 guidance: revenue between $212 million and $220 million, operating margin between 22% and 24%, non-GAAP diluted EPS between $0.49 and $0.55, with the sequential dip attributed to Chinese New Year (mid-February) holidays slowing customer tape-outs, expected to resume in early March; management sees no major change in the market environment and says design starts remain healthy and support the full-year growth trajectory. Visibility is limited with a typical backlog of only 1 to 3 weeks.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue between $212 million and $220 million; operating margin between 22% and 24%; non-GAAP EPS between $0.49 and $0.55; backlog 1 to 3 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Photronics continues to see growth in masks that support 'AI-driven chip packaging applications and masks for high NA EUV development projects', and expects high-end strength to continue. In the U.S., it is supporting high-volume manufacturing at 12 and 14-nanometer logic while extending qualifications to 8-nanometer and below, and for advanced DRAM is in qualification activity using new processes on its multi-beam mask writer for patterns below 20 nanometers.
quarterly_data.figure: HVM at 12 and 14-nanometer; qualifications to 8-nanometer and below; DRAM patterns below 20 nanometers

quarterly_data.signal: Expansion projects in the U.S. and Korea will enter volume production in 2027, as customers there pursue broader outsourcing strategies (increased captive outsourcing). Allen, Texas: cleanroom ready, tools delivered and being installed, customer qualifications expected to be completed by the second half of this year; Allen targets U.S. mainstream wafer fabs at 90-nanometer to 40-nanometer and will take middle/low-end loading off Boise so Boise capacity can be reserved for high-end business.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. and Korea volume production in 2027; Allen nodes 90-nanometer to 40-nanometer

quarterly_data.signal: Head of Asia operations said the high-end business is 'a little bit capacity constrained' rather than demand constrained: Photronics needs to maximize its most advanced (Boise) output and is working with many customers to qualify a new writer with much higher throughput, alongside Boise high-end capacity expansion to meet strong high-end customer demand.

Q1 CapEx was $48 million, mainly equipment to extend FPD technical leadership. Photronics reiterated fiscal 2026 CapEx guidance of $330 million, elevated by special project investments in the U.S. and Korea plus accelerated end-of-life tool upgrades; CFO expects added depreciation but also revenue from those projects and does not expect margins to 'fall off a cliff'. Cash and short-term investments rose $49 million sequentially to $637 million, including $459 million held in joint ventures in which Photronics holds a 50.1% interest.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 CapEx $48 million; fiscal 2026 CapEx guidance $330 million; cash $637 million ($459 million in 50.1%-owned JVs)

quarterly_data.signal: FPD revenue of $60 million rose 3% year-over-year, with a mix shift toward mainstream demand for larger-size China IT display projects. In Korea Photronics took delivery of the most advanced mask writer for the FPD market, as the first display mask supplier with that capability, targeting high-end AMOLED masks including G 8.6 size; G8.6 AMOLED is in its infancy with adoption expected to broaden later this year. Asked about G 8.6, Frank Lee said Photronics did receive 'a very first set of [indiscernible] photomask from our Korean customers' and sees many Chinese customers developing 8.6 AMOLED business.

China: Photronics focuses on high-end nodes through its Xiamen facility, serving major Chinese high-end wafer fabs, where the qualification burden keeps entry barriers for newcomers very high; new local entrants may pressure mainstream but management sees margins relatively flat or slightly improving. Asia demand is driven by geopolitical regionalization (design houses must make wafers at Chinese foundries to sell chips in China, causing a lot of duplicate work) and by Chinese customers migrating to 22-nanometer this year, producing many new tape-outs at 22, 28-nanometer.
quarterly_data.figure: new tape-outs in 22, 28-nanometer from China customers
